headline: Singapore Records Slower Income Growth And Higher Unemployment 2026
metaDescription: The Ministry of Manpower reports that Singapore saw slower real income growth and increased unemployment rates for non-PMET roles throughout 2026.
aiSummaryBullets: Median monthly incomes for full-time employees in Singapore grew to S$6,021 in 2026 from S$5,775 in 2025.
Advance figures from the Ministry of Manpower indicate that real income growth slowed over the past year.
Non-PMET roles experienced a higher rate of unemployment during the 2026 period.
aiContextParagraph: Advance data released by the Singaporean Ministry of Manpower highlights shifting labor market conditions for 2026. While nominal median monthly incomes for full-time employees increased to S$6,021, compared to S$5,775 in 2025, the report notes a deceleration in real income growth. Simultaneously, the labor market faced challenges regarding job security in specific sectors, with higher unemployment figures recorded among non-PMET workers. These findings offer an initial overview of the nation's economic performance and employment landscape as the year draws to a close. The ministry typically utilizes these advance figures to track annual workforce trends, providing insight into how economic adjustments are impacting salary progression and sectoral job availability across the country. Government agencies continue to monitor these developments to assess the broader implications for the national workforce.
whyItIsViral: The topic is trending due to significant public interest in economic indicators, underscored by high search volumes for unemployment and coverage by local news outlets.
